utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. While we're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, I'd like to deal briefly with two matters. First - and I'm addressing the Defence - the Chamber notes that on the 5th of September, the Defence filed a motion tendering 15 exhibits associated with the rule 92 ter statement of witness Sveto Veselinovic. The Chamber notes that the document listed as Exhibit 1D03099 is not on the Defence 65 ter exhibit list. Do you want to add that to your 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's the position of the Prosecution in relation to adding this document to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We have no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted. And with regard to the remaining exhibits associated with the statement of the witnesses, the Chamber invites the Defence to consider reducing the number of associated exhibits by for example tendering some of these documents with the witness during examination-in-chief. Would you consider that, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And I've already said to my colleague from the Prosecution that we would reduce that number, so we will have a lot less documents that we're going to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you, Mr. Sipovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, and my respects to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Lukic will now briefly re- examine you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Emphasis on briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's your emphasis, not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screen, P3753, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sipovac, while we're waiting for the document to appear on the screen, you will see on the document, once it appears, that this has to do with the subregion. And it says Sanski Most. To the best of your knowledge, in Sanski Most, was there a subregion of any kind?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of. I don't know what this is all about. I can read it out, but the abbreviation itself doesn't mean a thing to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Can we have page 2 in B/C/S now. At the bottom of the page, we see that there is no signature. There is a stamp of the SDS. Now I'd be interested in paragraph 4. In line 4, it says -- they're asking for the 1st Krajina Corps to be cleansed of Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "We believe that they cannot fight against their own people ..." During those first days of the war, after the conflict broke out, were there any demands made for people to be dismissed from units? Was there some wondering of this kind, say, in your unit?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my unit. Let me repeat what I said yesterday; all military conscripts, all able-bodied men aged 18 to 60, all of those who had war assignments, irrespective of ethnic background, in accordance with their VS, they had military obligation. They were conscripts. I've already said this yesterday. There was this permanent pressure of the policy of the SDA and the HDZ. There was this obstruction of mobilisation. Some people accepted this as such, whereas others did respond to the call-up. In principle, more people ignored mobilisation than responding to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have P3892, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of the command of the 1st Krajina Corps. Yesterday, this first part was read out to you where it says that the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina that a request is being made to remove officers who are ethnic Croats or Muslims. What about Prijedor? Were attempts made by the civilian authorities to establish their own TO units?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Units of the TO belonged to local communes. So how do I put this? They were really under the civilian authorities as opposed to war-time units, so that's the way it was. So, yes, through TO units. But directly war-time units, no, absolutely not. If that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain this to you. TO units were under the authority of the civilian authorities and they had greater powers over them. They reported to them and so on and so forth. Whereas, JNA units, war-time units, absolutely there were no units established on ethnic grounds, and it is not that the authorities could exercise any influence that level, local. However, it was different at political levels, republican level, federal level, and so on. That is higher political level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please let us try to be as brief as possible. We have a lot of material to cover.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, but you did ask me about all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have P3893 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the answer given by the witness is still somewhat unclear to me. He said that there were no units established on ethnic grounds. Were these the local units? Were you referring to the local units at that moment? Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said on ethnic grounds, that's what I was saying, I mean, the authority. I mean, the question was the authorities, whether the authorities could establish a unit and whether they could exercise influence. I think that was the question. So this was my answer. On the basis of the very concept and structure and the way in which commands were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, a long story. I asked you, you used the words "there were no units established on ethnic grounds." Were you referring to local units at this moment, or were you referring to units of a regional or a higher level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about Prijedor, at that moment. When I say on ethnic ground, I mean, I'm saying that the structures of authority now regardless of whether these are Serbs, Muslims, Croat, it didn't matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now you made clearly a distinction on where it was not possible and that, as you said, the higher political level that was different. Do I there understand that creating units or staffing or manning units at the higher level that you would not exclude that to be done on ethnic -- on an ethnic basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can exclude that. I mean, I'm talking only about the plans, the staffing plans, that I had. Not a single staffing plan envisaged the establishment of units on a ethnic basis rather it was on the basis of VES, that is to say, military specialty; somebody who had been trained for something, irrespective of training background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you made a distinction between the local level and the higher up level -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I have to understand that as far as ethnic composition of units, there was no difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no differences. Let me say that. There was no difference in terms of this approach I told you [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... a few lines ago, you made a distinction between the two levels but I now do understand that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'm -- I'm inviting you not to interrupt me. I now do understand that where you said a few lining that is there was a distinction that there was, in fact, no distinction. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sipovac, did you speak about the manning of your units, what you worked on or the TO units? Did you man the TO units?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only dealt with war-time units. The TO units, as I said a moment ago, were -- actually we were supposed to do this as the military department. But we did not man these units because this was under the authority of the municipal authorities. That's what I said to His Honour the Judge a moment ago. So this was done by the municipal structures of government, irrespective of who was in power, the SDA, the SDS, the Serb, a Croat, or a Muslim. This was really under their authority. Or rather, it wasn't under their authority. They didn't hand over the files to us and we were supposed to do this. It was part of our job description.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a document here and we see General Mladic's signature typed out here, so it's type-signed. And it says that officers of Muslim and Croat ethnicity must be sent on leave immediately and that action should be taken to refer them to the Army of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at once, in order to resolve their status in the service. First of all, when this document was shown to you, you mentioned an officer who was an ethnic Croat who asked for something and then you were interrupted at that point.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you briefly just tell us what it was that you wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Lukic, could you give us a page and line reference? I take it it was yesterday's transcript? If you have the words, that would allow me to search the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on and we'll come back to that. My colleague Ivetic will try to find in yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, officers who were Serbs, where did they resolve their status-related issues?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. I guess the interpretation was not good. And I didn't even hear all of it. I just heard Serbs, officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're supposed not to criticize our interpreter services which are of excellent quality and the claim that you are able to say that they are wrong, if you have any questions in relation to that, you may raise the matter. But you're supposed not to tell us that the interpreters are not doing their job properly. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't wish to criticize and I'm not criticizing the way they do their work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please allow me to say this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, witness. I read to you. You said I guess the interpretation was not good. That is criticizing the work of our interpreters, and I'm not, at this moment, allowing you to say anything more. Carefully listen to the question. If there's any translation issue, you may appropriately draw our attention to it and if there's any problem, Mr. Lukic also will --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm on English channel and probably I started to speak earlier so I -- I guess he was still receiving translation and I started to speak. That's why he didn't hear me correctly. It's my assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is appreciated that you take the blame for it but it doesn't change anything what I told the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Sipovac, at the time, officers who were ethnic Serbs, that is to say, on the 9th of June, 1992, when this document was written up, professional officers, where did they resolve their status-related issues?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They resolved them in Yugoslavia, these professionals, because they were all together in the Federal Secretariat for National Defence that had a personnel department for all professional officers in the JNA, and then there was this transformation of the JNA, and how do I put this? When these national armies came into being, Serbia, Croatia, Macedonia, Slovenia, that is, when the JNA broke up along ethnic lines, and then in -- Serbs resolved it in Belgrade and Banja Luka but, basically, the centre was the Federal Secretariat for National Defence in Belgrade, for all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, transcript page 28191, line 22 to 28192, line 16, you started to talk about an officer, a Croat ethnic officer. What was it that you wanted to say, sir?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to say that the senior officers submitted requests seeking a resolution of their status question in view of the JNA -- of the fact that it was reorganising, they were joining their national corps but they couldn't do it without the permission of their senior officer because then it would be something else. Although some of those did do that. I think this officer, Ante Fiamenko he was in the 43rd with us. He asked for an order to go to Belgrade to the SSNO where you wanted his status to be resolved. There was also a case where Ademi already in 1991 joined the Green Berets. Namely he left the JNA without anybody's permission at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have P217 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P217. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of the 1st Krajina Corps dated the 13th of June 1992. Item 6 was presented to you yesterday. This is on page 2 of the English and on page 5 in the B/C/S version in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have an issue with the translation on this matter. In English version, it says the "purging", and in B/C/S, it says "diferencijacija", differentiation. So there was English word for this, too. There was no need to change it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, if there's any translation issue then, of course, it should be sent to CLSS for verification. That's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you see in item 6, line 5 where it says "diferencijacija" [B/C/S spoken] differentiation of officers on an ethnic basis?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding this document and the previous document as well as others that were shown to you, was anybody ran out of the service in Prijedor in your area because of their ethnicity, any officers?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They could have asked for -- to leave. Nobody would have created any problems for them if they did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have 1D5277, please, and we do not have translation of these documents, since Mr. Sipovac brought them with him. [Interpretation] This is the first page, Mr. Sipovac --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could Mr. Sipovac also tell us, to start with, where it comes from, and why it was in his possession rather than in any archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sipovac, since there's no translation, could you please tell us the information that Judge Orie is seeking.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the preparation for this trial, as much as time permitted, I tried to prepare information that would contradict what Mr. Mesanovic was saying, that I was issuing orders to call up exclusively Serbs. As proof of the fact that there were members of other ethnic groups there, I asked the authorised municipal organ that has everybody's particulars, meaning the conscripts, to give me information and to note who were non-Serbs because that was the only organ that kept such a record, and on the basis of birth records, could determine a person's ethnicity, and that's the reason why I asked for that, Your Honours, and why I brought it with me. As for why this is such a brief period, I am very grateful that I'm able to testify earlier because I had some private commitments that I had to see to. I'm talking about this time-period, the 6th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who gave the document to you?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can you see in the heading it was the city of Prijedor, the city administration, the section for veterans' and invalids' benefits of Prijedor at my personal request. The reference is certified copies of Vob-2, Vob-8, and this is signed by the person who is assigned to these kinds of jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have the second page in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell us whose card this is.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the personal card of a reserve officer in this case. It says Marko Tomic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, according to the second page, without being told what the first page is about, I'm not able to follow what is happening on the first -- on the second page? I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First page is just a cover page. It's not part of the document. It just proves [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... explains what is going to happen with the things that are attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or does it not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Or does it not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please. That might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The reference certified copies, Vob-2, Vob-8 and PERS-7 to be delivered to in reference to your request we are sending you certified copies of units personnel files and exerts from Vob-8 for certain individuals upon request who were members of the armed forces of the SFRY-Republika Srpska. Enclosed 1 PERS-7 x 3, 2 Vob-2 x 11 and 3 excerpt from Vob-8 x 35 pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... before we can understand what the acronyms mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell us -- Mr. Sipovac, could you please tell us what PERS means, what Vob means, Vob-2 and Vob-8?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: PERS-7 means this is a personnel file of a reserve senior officer in the military records and there are three copies. Then Vob-2 x 11, this is the file of personnel they're all identical. They contain the particulars of persons who are either veterans or invalids. Identical cards or files were kept in the military units so the Vob means the military records of military conscripts and there are 11 of them, excerpt from Vob-8 is also a form a record of military conscripts. It's in the form of a book with some 11 or 12 sections. I'm not sure where the surname, father's name, Christian name, personal ID number, municipality, place of birth, war-time assignment, unit rank, military occupational specialty of the conscript that -- during the time he served his term of duty, date of joining the unit, date of leaving the unit, reason why he left the unit. And as far as I can remember, I don't have the forms, but I think that's more or less all the information that's contained in that form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I ask the witness whether he has made a written request to receive this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have a copy of that written request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I don't, and I realise that that was an error, and I even thought of asking them to fax it to me. I did it in handwriting but I -- I don't have it with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take that it is still kept somewhere because it might be important know on what basis the selection was made. Does the documentation which you now present, does that in any way is to be linked to the first half of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1991, 1992, and 1993 and all the other years, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you apparently you have looked at it. Could you perhaps then take the witness through the relevant portions where it specifically deals with the time-frame we are, at this moment, of course, primarily interested in. So as to better understand what it all is that the witness brings us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Can we have second page in this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sipovac, could you please tell us briefly something about Stipo Tomic, father's name Marko.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a captain first class by rank. On page 2 of the file you could see the duty he was assigned to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the first thing I'd like to hear from the witness where it refers to the relevant time-period. And if he has indicated that, then we'll hear what happened early 1992 or late 1991, rather than to start with the whole story about Mr. Tomic. First, focus on the time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As we look at the document, was Mr. Tomic a member of the armed forces in 1991 and 1992 and until when was he a member, if you know?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you open the file you can see the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. But there is no translation, so you need to explain that to us.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, just like that, until when, he was there. But it's there in the file. He was a member of the 43rd Motorised Brigade. On this page, you cannot see that information, but when you open it or look at the next page or something, then you will see the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, first of all, it would have been advisable that the witness does not engage in such inquiries himself but rather leave that to professionals. If there's no reference to the time-frame you're invited to get the relevant material because just to look at document and have a name, and if there's no link to the time-frame we're talking, then it doesn't assist the Chamber. And the answer, if you open the file, which we cannot do, because it is not there, it's just a seven-page document then please better prepare for that. Witness, when did you give this material to the Defence; could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before, a couple of days ago, when I came here. But if you permit me, Your Honour, a question, and a request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I -- I addressed Mr. Lukic on the matter, and I've now received an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the next page then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it assist you to look at this page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I take it you have looked at it as well, not only the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where do we find a reference to the time-frame we are primarily interested in. Because I see on the right page I see an entry at the bottom, 1978, further up, I see as the latest one, 1989. If there's anything else to be found on this page, I'd like to -- that you draw my attention to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And can I take it that in December 1989 there was this person be promoted to major? Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, the date. Are you asking me actually?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you. Is that -- is that about promotion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Promotion, yes, he was captain first class and then major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And what is does the date on the right-hand side in the last column mean, 2/90?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We ask the witness where we find a reference to either late 1991 or 1992 on this document. Witness, could you tell us where we find a reference to that time-frame?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the last page that cannot be seen here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then military exercises can be seen here and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic will take us to whatever page where we find a relevant link to the time-frame we are primarily focussing on. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those are pages I have for this Mr. Tomic. Four pages. And that's the document I have that was uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many pages are there? I just received four.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a form. It's two pages that are joined, so it's 1, 2, 3, 4 and then there should be participation in the war. It's not legible what I see here. Then on the last page -- well, it depends on when the personal file was typed up. There has to be another page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you have had an opportunity to look at this document for a couple of days. You know what you wanted to establish with this. And then the least I would expect you to do is to at least bring a link to the time-frame rather than to send us some documents of people who have served in the army somewhere in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we go one page up. So the -- actually, it's the second page in this document. Because I showed that one to the witness and he said he cannot see it on that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If can you see it -- I mean, it's not only -- you are asking questions about the document which you want to be in evidence, I take it. Then at least you should be aware of what you want to establish in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's clear for everyone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not for me. Explain to me what you want to establish and I'm happy to follow you in understanding what you wish to do. Let me then ask you: What are you about to establish with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sipovac, do you see here on the left-hand side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see this stamp here: Military obligation stopped --

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a very legible copy. I think it says military obligation stopped according to Article 234. It's hardly legible. And then it says: Erased from military records, but then the date cannot be seen ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which stamp are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was a stamp on the -- in the middle of the page in the left page, actually, there are two pages, left and right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we zoom onto it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, do you have a hard copy of this? Is that better legible?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have hard copy, but it's same like this. Only I -- I -- I can read 96. I don't know ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can read 96.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But he was -- it says in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 6 is that the last -- the letter the most to the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. [Interpretation] "Erased from military records. Official Gazette ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that is not in the stamp. Is that the words that are typed here. Not in the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's written. Handwritten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you again read what the stamp exactly says. And, again, this is not how we should do it nevertheless that may create some clarity. Where it says -- starts with the word "vojna".

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Military obligation stopped according to Article 234 of the Law on the Army, erased from military records, Official Gazette of the RS ..." I cannot see the number: "/96."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now what -- and I'm seeking now legal information. What does Article 234 tell us? I'm not asking you to testify but to give me information about a relevant legal provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You expect me to know laws by heart, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I expect you to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have that law in front of me. We can ask this witness. Maybe he will know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can do so, but on legal -- if you present this document and if you want to rely on this stamp, I would have expected you to at least check what Article 234 says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... This gentleman has personal knowledge. I wanted to ask him if he knows that that gentleman was in the VRS during the war. So it is personal knowledge. It's better than the document and the document it says he is -- he was not -- he was not in the document after '96.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are telling us that you don't know what Article 234 [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Mr. Sipovac, what Article 234 is about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has to do with a person's military service ceasing due to his age. He no longer had military obligation. All of that doesn't really matter. What matters is how long he participated in the war and then I see down here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... witness, what matters and what doesn't matter is for the parties to decide. Please, answer the questions. Do you have any personal knowledge about this person, because that's what Mr. Lukic is hinting at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Lukic will ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you do, Mr. Lukic, when the witness originally directed us to this corner of the stamp, the idea was to come and look for a date that connects this document to the period in issue here, 1991, 1992. I still am not finding that connection here. I'd like to be guided as to what we are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sipovac, how should we understand this document? What do you see on it? What is written here? Can you help us with this?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I'd like to say. The Presiding Judge asked me whether I knew anything about this man, and this is the answer I can provide. The man was assistant for morale and religious affairs and later on in the brigade command. And I don't think that he stayed throughout the war. I saw that in his documentation. It must be here and I cannot see this very clearly here. Maybe it was handwritten down here and that hardly be read. The date is not legible. But he was certainly in the war, and he was the assistant for morale guidance and religious affairs, and I don't think that he stayed in the brigade throughout. I think that sometime in 1994, since he had a special profession, I think that he was transferred to work obligation. However, it would have to be in the column where it says military exercises or something. There are dates for everyone. So he'd have to be included. So this information is handwritten. Perhaps it's more legible in another one of the files that we will be looking at, so then we will see. And the file shows that he is of Croat ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock. I didn't emphasise the brief when we started. I, however, do now. This is a chaotic presentation of evidence. Could you please try to conclude as soon as possible. And let's not forget: You have had a couple of days to look at this documentation so as to come to a focussed presentation of evidence of this witness. The Chamber looks at it only since the last 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can tell you that we worked all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not blaming you for not working, but I'm expecting you to present this evidence in such a way that it reflects the opportunity you had for a couple of days to look at this material. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D5276, please. It's the same cover page as before, since we divided the documents that we received from Mr. Sipovac into three documents, so the same cover page and attached is the document on the second page, so if we can have the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What kind of book is this?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a list of military personnel for all persons who were spent in a unit during war and the reasons why they left the unit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the last sentence. Could you repeat those, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the front page of a book, Vob-8, where a list is kept of military conscripts, or, rather, military personnel, for the time that they spent in war-time units and that has to do with participation in the war and it includes information that I referred to when I was asked about what the abbreviation Vob-8 meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what is written here is: "List of military personnel; unit, 43rd Prijedor Motorised Brigade." The date from which it has been kept, the 16th of September, 1991, and the time when the -- the date when the list is concluded, the 30th of March, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 4 now. Actually, page 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Say the fifth name from the bottom up. It says, "Begic, Franjo".

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Son of Dragan".

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can ethnicity be seen on this list?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But in his file, it can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. My colleague the Prosecutor, he made an observation, when we looked at the first and second books, we noticed that the last names stop with the letter S. Do you know why? Is this the complete documentation that you have? My colleague said Z, Zeljaja, that should be --

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, really. When we speak about records, I looked at random samples. That's what I asked for. Say, 14, 15.000 persons that are registered in the records --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the records are not complete?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, it's not that I made this selection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So let us remember this name: Franjo Begic, son of Dragan. And now let us look at the next document, 1D5278. So it's the same first page. And we need page 8 of this document. What is this? What is this document? What is it that we see?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a file of a military conscript that is kept by the Secretariat for National Defence and there is an identical document except that it says: Unit card or file. And that is kept in the unit where his war-time assignment was. The units or, rather, the documents that are kept in the unit and in this file have to be identical, so everything is there: Address, promotions, decorations. There are two types of information that are provided. Those that cannot be changed and those that can be changed. For example, address, residence. That can be changed. Whereas, the date of birth, et cetera, cannot be changed. So I'm reading out here Begic, Dragan, Franjo. I see ethnicity, date of birth and then further down here there is other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 25 says participation in the war.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of the page, very bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at line 25. It says participation in the war.

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 25. It says military post code 7362. This person came on the 30th of September, 1992, and this person left on the 7th of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Lukic's question or the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the date when this person joined was the 30th of September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And when this person left, that date is the 7th of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And line 6, line 6. What is entered there?

utterances.speaker: CEDO SIPOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't see that. Ethnicity, it says, Croat. If you're thinking of item 6. Ethnicity: Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm looking at the clock. We would just ask for all those three documents to be MFI'd. We would have another witness who will be able to talk in more details about these documents. I only wanted to introduce them through Mr. Sipovac since he brought them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No objection to them being MFI'd, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. Do we have all the three numbers, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour we do. It's -- first, it's 1D5276. 1D5277. And 1D5278.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you assign numbers for them to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D5276 receives number D767. Document 1D5277 receives number D768. And document 1D5278 receives number D769, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All three are marked for identification. Could I -- were these your last questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I had a couple of more, but minding the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like to thank Mr. Sipovac for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you have any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this concludes your testimony, Mr. Sipovac. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, questions put to you by the party, or questions put to you by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you permit me, Your Honours, I have a request. I would like to shake the hand of General Mladic, if the protocols permit that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The protocol does not permit that. And neither does the protocol permit Mr. Mladic to speak aloud. You may follow the usher. But it is clear to Mr. Mladic that you expressed that wish and that may mean something to him. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before we take the break, I must confess that I'm a bit confused. Because I thought that what we heard from this witness that it all started with documentation which said non-Serbs should not be active in the army and the matter being settled in Belgrade, and now we end up with a conscript which apparently joined in late September 1992 and stayed until 1995, not being an officer. So I'm wondering what exactly we have been listening at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness, through his statement and testimony, actually told us that there are more than 100 non-Serbs only in his brigade who joined the Army of Republika Srpska. So there was some officers in the command. Those three gentlemen were separated in one document as officers, and we can see on this list, but I wanted to go with him through the list. It would be much faster but he is very cautious about expressing himself on anybody's nationality. So he said no, you have to go through personal -- those -- well, personal lists, so only there you can check if somebody is Croat, Muslim, or Serb. So we'll have probably to -- we started to go the other way, so to show that in this 43rd Brigade, Prijedor Brigade there were more than 100 non-Serbs out of 700, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now I understood the position of the Prosecution to be that there was documentation which hinted at, let's get rid of them. But at the same time hesitation that it would result in shortage of staffing, and that for that reason that the intention was not immediately well, could not be complied with immediately although the -- underlying thought would still be there. Therefore, I'm asking myself to what extent does the one contradict the other? You say they were still there. Prosecution, as far as I understand, says they intended to do A, but there were hesitations which may have resulted in them still being there. That's how I understood the exchange of evidence and I'm wondering where exactly where the one position contradicts the other. What is really in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The dispute is actually that our position is whoever wanted to stay, stayed. Nobody was forced to leave. We are actually in the process of acquiring and translating more documents where we would see there were many more members of VRS of non-Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't understand that it's the position of the Prosecution that there were no non-Serbs anymore but there was a clear intention to have them out as soon as circumstances would allow for that. That's my understanding of the position of the Prosecution. Yes, Mr. Traldi. You are hiding behind the column, but.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. It's our position that there was a clear intention and that many were removed. It's not the Prosecution's position that there were literally zero non-Serbs in the VRS. But it is our position, certainly, that a number were removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the real issue is were people removed and -- on ethnic grounds not leaving voluntarily. That's one and the second is what proportions are we talking about. That seems to be the matter in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That seem like an accurate summary to me, if Mr. Lukic agrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if that's the dispute, then, of course, we'd like to receive focussed evidence which directly relates to that issue in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we received the evidence from Mr. Malcic as well and he testified on this issue and -- so that's actually our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least we have now identified what seems to be in dispute. And let's take a break of 22 minutes and resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to call its next witness? Mr. Stojanovic and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sveto Veselinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. May I remind the Defence that there are still a few notices to be filed about changing the status from confidential -- from public to confidential in relation to witnesses on certain matters, there was some witness protection. So I think for -- including for Mr. Veselinovic but I think for another six, the Chamber is still waiting for those notices to be filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Chamber may have noticed that Ms. Stewart is not present. She is called to other duties in another courtroom, so I'd like to introduce Sebastiaan van Hooydonk who is here in her place and I would also introduce Amir Zec, who is counsel that you will be seeing in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, those who are new in the courtroom - not everyone is new - welcome. Mr. Veselinovic, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Veselinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Veselinovic, you will first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we begin?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the procedure here, I would like you to, with slow words, speak your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Sveto Veselinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veselinovic, did you provide a statement to the Defence of Radovan Karadzic? And did you answer in writing questions that they put to you?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at document 65 ter 1D04290 in e-court, please. Could we also look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, is this your signature on the document and is the date written in pencil written in your hand?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at item 1 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, did you tell me while preparing for your testimony today, that the last two sentences would need to be reformulated in order to clarify further your statement in such a way that they read: "After the first multi-party elections, I was elected a member of the Executive Committee of the municipality with the specific assignment of being the chief of the municipal administration for revenue." Would the last two sentences, the way I have read them, be correct rather than the way it is written in your statement right now?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now that we have made this correction, I would like to ask you if you were asked the same questions today after giving your solemn declaration as you were asked then, would you give the same answers, and would those answers be complete, truthful, and accurate?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender the witness's statement with the 65 ter number 1D04290. This is the statement of Witness Veselinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D4290 receives number D770, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like us to move into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I would like to read the summary of Witness Veselinovic 's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness Sveto Veselinovic is a Ph.D. degree-holder in economic sciences and he is one of the founders of the SDS in Rogatica. After the founding assembly for the SDS party for the municipality of Rogatica, he was elected as president of the party in Rogatica. Following the first multi-party elections, he was elected member of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Rogatica and his specific assignment was the chief of the municipal administration for public revenue. He will speak about attempts to set up organs of power in Rogatica, about problems and lack of understanding between the ethnic groups, about the different approach to mobilisation, as well as about the forming of the Crisis Staff of the SDS in Rogatica, with the task of monitoring the situation in the field. This Crisis Staff had different tasks than the Crisis Staff of the Rogatica municipality, which also had a different composition in terms of personnel. In March 1992, the witness resigned from all of his posts because he believed that problems could be resolved with negotiations as opposed to the position of the TO, and they did not have the mandate to lead the Serbian people to war. After that, a new Crisis Staff was elected, at the head of which was Mile Sokolovic. The witness became a member of this Crisis Staff too. His task was -- actually, their task was to conduct negotiations regarding the separation of the territory of the municipality of Rogatica and the division of power. With the killing of Drazenko Mihajlovic in May 1992, these efforts were suspended and major clashes broke out and refugees began to arrive. In order to resolve their status, the Crisis Staff formed a commission to receive and take care of the refugees, and the witness was appointed at the head -- as the head of this body.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Due to increasing insecurity in the town and street fighting, both Serbs and Muslims began to leave the town and move out. At the same time, more and more Serb refugees were arriving in Rogatica, and it was necessary to provide accommodation for them. The witness was the first to enter Rogatica following the withdrawal of the Muslim forces from the town, and after he saw many destroyed buildings, the hotel, the synagogue, the transformer station, the mosque, his father-in-law's house and his brother's house, he documented all of this in a video recording where one can see, amongst other things, the fortifications that the Muslim side used in these battles. The witness will also give his comments on the statements of certain people who had mentioned him and who had referred to certain information about Rogatica which the witness believes are simply not accurate. This was the summary of this witness statement, Your Honour, and with your leave, I would like to put a few questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veselinovic, in paragraph 18 of your statement, you say that after heavy fighting and the death of 13 Serbs, you entered town for the first time. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber from which direction you entered the town of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I entered town from the northern part of Rogatica. That is to say, from the malt factory, Sladara, where the Crisis Staff of the Serb Municipality of Rogatica was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your assessment and to the best of your recollection, what was the time when this occurred?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was five or six days after the liberation of Rogatica or, rather, after the Muslims left Rogatica. If we're speaking in terms of dates, it was the very end of July; the 29th, the 30th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who actually recorded on video the clips that you referred to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I personally recorded that with my own camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there anyone else there with you then?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had a colleague there who drove my car while we were driving through town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, when you were reading the summary of the witness statement, you said, at page 35, line 18 that the witness was the first to enter Rogatica following the withdrawal of the Muslim forces from the town. I see from the statement that he says when he first entered the town, not that he was the first to enter the town. I guess what is in the statement is the correct version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what I suppose too, but with your leave, perhaps we should ask the witness which one is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So is it correct - this is my question - were you the first person who entered town, or, as your witness says [as interpreted]: "After I entered town for the first time, after the Muslims had left," and so on?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot claim that I was the first one who entered up to that is to say when the Muslims left, first of all, it was military formations that were in town and the police of Republika Srpska. As the army withdrew into the barracks, the police stayed on and was in control of town. For a certain period of time, perhaps 15 or 20 days even, the police did not allow civilians to enter town, not even the Crisis Staff, without their approval. So as far as civilians are concerned and members of the Crisis Staff, I am one of the first persons who had the approval to enter town because in the Crisis Staff, I was the person who was in charge of refugees and abandoned property.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Thank you for your assistance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry. I apologise for interrupting. I notice the witness appears to have a couple of papers with him, including some handwritten notes, and I'm curious what they might be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us what documents you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I have before me is the statement that I provided and in order for it to be easier for me to find my way through these paragraphs, I have something handwritten, what each paragraph is about briefly. And, of course, I have my original documents that I submitted along with this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put all that away. If you need to consult your statement, a clean copy will be given to you. But without my approval, without the Chamber's approval, you're not allowed to consult any documents. And if you need to consult, please address me first. So would you please put them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could we please take a look at an excerpt from a document, 65 ter 1D5280.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's no soundtrack, and it would run from 1:20 until 1:37. It's a video. It's a video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to ask you to answer a few questions once we've seen this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court what town this is and what was recorded here specifically?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: This is the centre of the town of Rogatica. I entered town in a car, and the first video recordings were made from a car. I was filming the very centre of town. You could see the destruction in town here. You could see destroyed shop windows, looted shops. Quite simply, everything was destroyed after the Serbs entered town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now the same video recording, the same document, let us take a look at 12:29 to 12:34. So it's 5 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, could you tell us what we have before us in this video-clip?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: This is my wife's family home. We see that it had been torched but this huge grass in front of the house shows that the burning did not take place recently, when Rogatica was being liberated. Rather, it was done considerably earlier when the Muslims were in control. Next to my wife's house, practically all other houses were torched. Those that were in the centre of town. Also quite a few apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now take a look at the following clip. From the same document, that is. From 16:32 up until 17:00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'd just like to ask you to tell us where this is. What is the location of this area that is documented in this video-clip?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: This is a residential building in the centre of town, and we call it Trg, and we see their machine-gun nest on top of this building that is facing the houses around it, and you can see damaged and destroyed roofs. So it's not that war was waged against an unknown enemy, someone who had come from elsewhere. This was a war between people who had lived together up until then in the same town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now take a look at the same video-clip but just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please, I would like to have the last still back. The witness said we can see the machine-gun nest. It's not there yet. Here. Could you please describe in more detail where we have to find the machine-gun nest you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if we were to start this, we'd see some type of machine-gun there - I don't know what kind of when it is - that was on the top of this residential building. I don't know whether the weapon worked, whether they left it there, and why they left it, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You made this comment when looking on this still in front of you now. Can you indicate where, on which roof of which house the machine-gun nest was located? Or is it -- was it on another still?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was right next to me or behind me. Because this was taken from the place where the barrel of that weapon was facing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps in order to clarify this. Can we go just a few seconds back so that we see -- this -- is this what you're referring to, or is that the same roof?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So now, please, from the same video-clip, same document number, could we take a look at 19:26 up until 20:15.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell the Court what it is that you recorded here and what this is? This part of the footage.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: This is the very centre of town. First you saw the building that had been torched where there were three Serb apartments; inter alia, my brother's apartment. Then you saw the hotel that had also been torched. And then could you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You were being asked what we see on the screen, not what we have seen before. Please tell us what we see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the screen, we saw a torched building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The question is what can be seen right now.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: These are mannequins in the window of a shop in that first building that we saw where the word "Promet" was written.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us just try to clarify this. Also in the same video-clip, can we see 21:34 to 22:10, very briefly. 21:34 to 22:10.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the first part of this video-clip, we saw a building. Could you please give us your comments on what kind of building this is?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: That is the city mosque that was destroyed in the town of Rogatica. There were two otherwise. This is one of the two. I think that this was the older one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then we see again a piece of weaponry, and I want to ask you whether that's the same machine-gun that we saw during the previous video-clip.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether the machine-gun is the same make, if that's what you're referring to, but this is a different machine-gun nest, and you saw that this was within the same footage, and it's only 30 metres from the mosque as the crow flies. So you could see how the mosque had been hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, could we now briefly move into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I repeat that we take a break now for 20 minutes. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I would like us to move into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Just for the record, I repeat in open session that the video we looked at earlier, it was admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we have another five documents admitted as associated exhibits, 65 ter numbers 1D03099; 1D04294, supporting paragraph 10 of the statement; 1D04296, supporting paragraph 16 of the statement; 1D04298, supporting paragraph 9 of the statement; and 1D05279, supporting paragraph 16 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3099 receives number D774. Document 1D4294 receives number D775. Document 1D4296 receives number D776. Document 1D4298 receives number D777. And document 1D5279 receives number D778, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D774 up to and including D778 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We'd like to thank the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this concludes our examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Traldi, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Veselinovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find him to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were the first president of the SDS in Rogatica. You held that position until the 25th of March, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 1D04293.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is an article published in Politika in 1991. You discuss it in your statement. At the bottom of the first page in the English and in the first column of the primary article in the centre of the page in B/C/S, the third paragraph, you're quoted by name. Now, you're referred to as president of the Rogatica SDS and chairman of the SDS Regional Board for Romanija. My first question is simply: You were also the chairman of the SDS Regional Board for the Romanija area; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, at the end of the paragraph you state: "However, we have a message for all those who are preparing dirty war plans that the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina are ready and that 1941 will never be repeated." When you spoke of 1941, you were referring to the mass murders of Serbs, Jews, and gypsies, among others, in Yugoslavia during the Second World War; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Was it common that when speaking in your official capacity, you would give public statements suggesting that the Serb people in Bosnia might imminently be subjected to mass murder?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see that there's anything in dispute there. If you wish to hear a more detailed explanation, after 1945, the Serb people lived together with other peoples in a common state and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm going to stop you and ask you to focus on my question. All I'd asked you was: Was it common for you when speaking in your official capacity, and by that I mean as a representative of the SDS, to make public statements suggesting that the Serb people in Bosnia might imminently be subjected to mass murder.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Events made it incumbent upon me to state something like that because in Communism the Serb people quite simply lived together with the Muslims. Yet again there was brotherhood and the same thing could have happened yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly that your answer is, yes, this is the sort of public statement that you often made at that time?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Public statements I did not make very often. I mean, I did not appear in public very often. But whenever there would be a situation in which one could clearly see the direction in which things were moving, I did warn against something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter 1D04293.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we decide on that -- Witness, do I understand that you do not deny that you expressed yourself in the way as published in this article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not my practice, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I wasn't asking whether it was your practice. It was -- you're quoted here. Does it reflect what you said at the time? At this instance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is a reflection of the situation that was developing at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it reflects your words, if I understand you well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D4293 receives number P6906, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, next, I'm going to play for you a conversation you had with President Karadzic in September 1991. It's a several-minute long intercepted conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, for the record, I'm going to ask that Mr. van Hooydonk play 65 ter 20280.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll now play it for a second time, and it may take quite some additional time for the interpreters to -- to tell us what is heard in the original. Witness, we'll play it for a second time. The interpreters were available to verify whether the transcript - I take it you've provided the transcript, Mr. Traldi - accurately reflects the words spoken so you will hear it for a second time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] "Unidentified Female: Hello, yes, can I help you. "Sveto: Tell me, may I talk to Dr. Karadzic. "A Female NN: What you did say, your name was? Sveto, right? "Sveto: Yes. "A Female NN: Just a moment. "Sveto: Hello. "A Male NN: Hello, Sveto. "Sveto: Tell me. "A Male NN: Could you wait for just a moment? The doctor is on the other line. "Sveto: Okay. "A Male NN: How is it over there towards Visegrad? "Sveto: Well, so-so. "A Male NN: Is that so? "He's about to finish this. He'll be with you in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear Dr. Karadzic in the background what he is saying.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Radovan KARADZIC: Hello? "Sveto: Good afternoon. "Radovan KARADZIC: Good afternoon, Sveto. "Sveto: Doctor, Risto told me to call you. "Radovan KARADZIC: We should be in touch all the time. What's the situation up there? "Sveto: Well, so-so. Nothing much. Those from Han Pijesak, our reservists, have taken up positions from Rogatica to Mesici. "Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. "Sveto: In Rogatica, reserve police forces are getting mobilised. "Radovan KARADZIC: Good. "Sveto: We have sent our men to joined the reserve force as well. "Radovan KARADZIC: By all means. "Sveto: So they don't do something stupid to surprise us. "Radovan KARADZIC: Absolutely, definitely. "Sveto: We're ready. We're waiting to see what happens next "Radovan KARADZIC: Good. Can you help Visegrad? "Sveto: We can. "Radovan KARADZIC: Do that, get in touch and let them take up positions at Sjemec up there, let them help prepare -- let them prepare to help Visegrad because if they start the war they'll start it against the people and against the army. "Sveto: Yes. I've already agreed to meet with Brano at Sjemec tonight. "Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. Good. It should ... and the column is waiting there, Sixty vehicles. Tomorrow the column is going to be enormous. Several kilometres to pass through Visegrad. Because the army won't yield. Are you in touch? Look, Zoran Vujovic can't get through to you at all. "Sveto: Well, I've been calling him. He is neither at home nor at work. "Radovan KARADZIC: Please call him. He said that some man at the number you had given him would not speak to him. "Sveto: I know nothing about it. "Radovan KARADZIC: Who is that? "Sveto: I don't know at all. "Radovan KARADZIC: I beg your pardon? "Sveto: Well, I don't know anything either. Me, neither ...
