"Radovan KARADZIC: Wait. The phone number you gave out. "Sveto: Well, I had given him my number. "Radovan KARADZIC: So how come he ... "Sveto: He must have taken down the wrong number. "Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. You see, he may have taken the wrong number but he cannot get in touch with you in any way. Tell me what is your situation. If it is difficult, should we sen from somewhere else to help you? "Sveto: No need for now, no need for right now. At Sjemec, we'll prepare it all for helping them if necessary. This evening, Brano and I will meet up there. "Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. Yes, yes. "Sveto: No problem, whatsoever. "Radovan KARADZIC: Good. And the police should help too; they'll co-operate with the police for as long as they are treating the military properly. You must not do anything against the military. No discussion. The army must pass through Visegrad. "Sveto: Shall we ... "Radovan KARADZIC: The army is not going to clean up ... they'll destroy Visegrad, they will not give in. So they should know that. "Sveto: Will the military now turn across Sjemec? It is critical down there through the tunnels. "Radovan KARADZIC: It is critical through the tunnels, is it? "Sveto: Eight tunnel. They can place a rocket launcher anywhere in the tunnel, destroy the first transporter, and block it. "Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh, good. Call Zoran, call the garrison in Uzice and suggest that they should go across Sjemec. However, they still have to go through Visegrad, right? "Sveto: They don't have to. "Radovan KARADZIC: They don't have to, instead ... "Sveto: Via Rogatica, to Ustipraca and Gorazde. "Radovan KARADZIC: How come they can't go to Visegrad? Where will they cross the river? "Sveto: Well, in Ustipraca. They're bypassing Visegrad ... "Radovan KARADZIC: Good. "Sveto: They're bypassing through Medjedja. "Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. "Sveto: The Drina canyon. "Radovan KARADZIC: Good, and where are they going to cross the Drina river? "Sveto: Across Drina they'll cross Drina in Ustipraca. It's 12 kilometres between Ustipraca and Gorazde. No tunnels, no attacks. "Radovan KARADZIC: So it was him who was shooting from that side of the river, is it? "Sveto: Yes. "Radovan KARADZIC: In Rudo, is it? Not Rudo, but ... "Sveto: No, no. From Visegrad go across Sjemec, across Borika to Rogatica and from Rogatica to Gorazde. "Radovan KARADZIC: Well, okay, but you have to go through Visegrad? "Sveto: You don't. "Radovan KARADZIC: You don't? "Sveto: In fact you do. Yes, yes. "Radovan KARADZIC: Well, you have to go through Visegrad. That's ... "Sveto: You have to go through Visegrad. "Radovan KARADZIC: You secure Visegrad because that is the narrow point and then the rest. Let them decide to go across Sjemec. "Sveto: Yes. "Radovan KARADZIC: Get in touch with -- you have to get in touch with the garrison and with this -- and they're looking for you. They cannot get through to in any way. Is Kusic there somewhere? "Sveto: Doctor, Kusic is down-town somewhere. "Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh, okay. And where are you? "Sveto: I'm at home at the moment. "Radovan KARADZIC: Uh-huh. Come on, please, do that and make sure they provide you duty service over there. "Sveto: Everything has been provided as far as it concerns our work. "Radovan KARADZIC: And a full, full, full, mobility of the party. Full mobility of everything. All the forces that you have. Everything you have. If necessity, add the Romanija forces too. "Sveto: Okay, boss. "Radovan KARADZIC: All right. "Sveto: All right, agreed."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, that was a long conversation but I have some very specific questions for you? First, the voices we just heard were your voice and President Karadzic's voice; right.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This conversation was about mobilising Serbs in Rogatica in September 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I think the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Kusic that's mentioned during the intercept, that's Rajko Kusic; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You refer --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please switch all the unnecessary mics off, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You refer to President Karadzic at the end as "boss." He was in fact your superior in the party; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the president of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 20280.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 20280 receives number P6907, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. I do not know where the sound comes from which is not there if the witness speaks, but and I'll switch off my microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It may have to do with the audio recording we had previously. Perhaps that can be removed and the sound, the background sound would perhaps disappear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That appears to be quite correct. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going ask you some general questions now about your political positions. As Mr. Stojanovic set out earlier, you were a member of both the SDS Crisis Staff in Rogatica in December -- established in December 1991 and the Crisis Staff established in April 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You also served as a member of the Rogatica Municipality War Commission; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the term "War Commission." Crisis Staff is one thing, Crisis Staff of the SDS, and then the Crisis Staff of the Rogatica municipality. And then after that, the Executive Board of the Rogatica municipality, where I was the chief of the public revenue administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's the Executive Board of the Rogatica Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I want to turn to your resignation in late March and could the Prosecution have P6823.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. P6823.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we read here in the first paragraph that: "The Crisis Staff of the SDS Municipal Board Rogatica is not able to carry out its decisions due to a group of armed Serbs, headed by a member of the Main Board SDS BiH Rajko Kusic, who was ruthlessly rushing with threats to attack into the town, in case that municipality and the public security station are not unconditionally divided into Serbian and Muslim parts within two hours' time." When you say in paragraph 14 of your statement that you resigned, in part, because of pressure from the Territorial Defence, it was these threats you were referring to; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the next paragraph reads: "The Crisis Staff, in compliance with your instructions, believes that the factual division on the ground should be and is already there ..." And I'm going to stop there. When you say "your instructions," you mean instructions from the SDS Main Board; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, instructions from the Main Board to monitor the situation and to report on the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to test your evidence on a that a little bit because that's not what you're describing here. You're saying: In compliance with your instructions, we believe that the factual division on the ground should be and is already there. So you had also received instructions regarding establishing a factual division on the ground, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: The division had always been there. There were always purely Serbian and purely Muslim villages. It was only the towns that in time became mixed-population towns. In order to avoid combat, in order to avoid conflicts, we agreed with the Muslims about the division, and we worked towards that division. We were negotiating at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll get to that division in a moment, sir, but I'd put to you that what you're saying here is that the factual division on the ground is in compliance with the SDS's instructions. That's true, isn't it? That's what you're saying in this letter.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you could conclude that on the basis of the letter, but as I said, even without the instructions, we worked on the division of the terrain only in order to prevent conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the final paragraph you mention that you'll be putting yourself at the disposal of the Yugoslavia national army. In Rogatica at that time, that the meant the 216th Mountain Brigade of the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: There was a Han Pijesak corps Brigade. It's possible, the 216th. I'm not sure which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: There was a battalion of that brigade in Rogatica; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. It was some 10 to 15 kilometres away from Rogatica in the Sjemec mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So that's 10 to 15 kilometres away from Rogatica town but within Rogatica municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, municipality of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And shortly after sending this letter, you joined that battalion; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was commanded by a Major Radomir Furtula?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the battalion went to Sarajevo in early May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you left your unit before it went to Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I was called by the newly formed Crisis Staff and told that I was appointed a member of that staff, and I received a new mobilisation post as member of the Crisis Staff, and I stayed in Rogatica in the Crisis Staff. I did not leave for Sarajevo with the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D04299.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is the mobilisation order you received; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see in the preamble that you're mobilised pursuant to a decision by the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: The Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbian municipality of Rogatica Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, the part that I was focussing on just to be clear, it says you're being mobilised pursuant to the provisions of a decision, and then it gives the name, taken by the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 20th of May, 1992. That's correct; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff made this decision. The decision was adopted on the basis of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not catch the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were already -- you'd already been appointed a member of the Crisis Staff at the beginning of April; correct? Specifically the 8th of April.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: No. On the 8th of April, a meeting was held of the Municipal Board of the Serbian Democratic Party. I didn't attend this meeting because I had submitted my resignation. Then the posts were verified for new members of the Crisis Staff to join it, meaning prominent Serb citizens from Rogatica who, up until that time, were not very involved. Mile Sokolovic was appointed as the number one man, and then he later worked --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: -- in certain activities and then he informed me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the interpreters told us that they did not catch the date. I'm not quite certain whether your follow-up questions have repaired that or not. Could you please have a look at page 66, line 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yeah, I was simply reading the date in the document which is why I hadn't followed up on it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then -- so apparently you repaired that shortcoming. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, before moving on, I would tender this document currently on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D4299 receives number P6908, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6908 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you hadn't quite -- I wasn't sure of your answer - let me say it that way - to my last question. You were a member of the Crisis Staff that was established on the 8th of April, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I did not attend that meeting. By that time, I had already reported to the unit. I received the information later and learned that I had been appointed a member of the Crisis Staff. Then in late April, I reported to my job. It wasn't right away on the 8th of April because I didn't even know then that I had been nominated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But you were, in fact, appointed on the 8th of April, as you learned later; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in your statement -- I'm turning to a different topic now and I'm done with this document. In your statement, you discuss the Rogatica Serb TO formed by Rajko Kusic. It was quickly placed under the control of the JNA; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, again, that would have meant the 216th Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know how that was in the organisational terms, whether it was the 216th or the Rogatica Brigade. In any event, later, going through these documents, I saw that sometime in late May, the unit was accepted as a part of the JNA, but I didn't know that at that point in time. I don't know the exact date, but I know it was sometime by the end of September, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now when you said late May, of course, the unit was accepted as part of the VRS, not the JNA at that time; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: We would need to look at the exact dates as to when the JNA withdrew officially from the B and H. I think that that was in June; whereas, this was in May, which means that it was accepted before the withdrawal of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'd put to you the Chamber's received a great deal of evidence on this. But if I suggest to you that the JNA withdraw on the 19th of May, would that refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: The 19th of May... I don't know. I don't know. We would need to look at the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I'll --

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I accept --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll leave the point there then, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 08778.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a bulletin issued by the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Ministry of Interior dated 24th of March, 1992. If we could turn to page 2 in both languages, the third paragraph, we see a report from Rogatica involving a man named Ismani Sasire, and I apologise for my pronunciation. That's a Muslim name; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: It's an Albanian name, a Siptar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see that four armed persons in camouflage uniform led by Rajko Kusic had, according to this report, stopped and maltreated this person and took away his vehicle. My question for you is: Is this the type of reckless behaviour that you were describing in your letter to President Karadzic when you spoke about Mr. Kusic?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know about this information at that time, the 23rd of March, we submitted the report before we resigned on the 25th of March. I didn't know about this at that time. And that was not a crucial factor. It was more his manner of asking that we stop with the negotiations because he had information in view of the fact that Alija rejected Cutileiro's plan in Lisbon on the 23rd of March, and so according to his information, they were speedily preparing for war, that they were just dragging things out through the negotiations that they were planning the liquidation of prominent Serbs in the course of one night --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: -- and so they were heading for war but we did not have the mandate to do something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think you've gone beyond the question that I asked slightly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions on this topic and I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 8778 receives number P6909, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6909 is admitted. I'm looking at the clock. Mr. Traldi, before we start with anything new, would this be a suitable time to take a break so that we would have left 35 minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It would be suitable for me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take a break. Could the witness follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, returning briefly to one of your last answers before the break. At temporary transcript page 69, line 1, I'd asked you about the name of a person named Ismani Sasire. And you said it's an ethnic Albanian name which you described using the term Siptar. Was that a term you commonly use?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: That's what we call themselves. Albanians in Kosovo call themselves Siptar. If somebody thinks that this a derogatory term it's not. That's what we call themselves and when they communicate between and amongst themselves, they use that name. Albanians from Kosovo, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think you have answered, perhaps, two or three other questions that I had in mind but not the one I actually asked. Which was simply, is that a term you commonly use yourself?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: For Albanians in Kosovo, that is what everybody in my area calls them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Including you, Witness? Because that was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not directly answer the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to move away from that topic now. You mentioned earlier today that when you were at the Crisis Staff you worked in the Sladara building. How often were you at the Sladara building, about how many times a week, in the months of May and June 1992?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: That was my workplace. I was there every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31593.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is Official Note of an interview you had with the Rogatica police in 2004. Did you tell the truth during that interview?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: They spoke to me. While we were talking and having coffee, they did not take any notes. I did tell them the truth, of course. These are people who knew the truth even apart from that talk that we had. Now how they perceived this, what I said to them, how they came to say that up until September I was in the army, I don't know. I did not see this after they had written this up. When they actually wrote this up, I don't know, how much later. They did not give this to me to sign. Had they asked me to sign this, I wouldn't have want to sign this. But this was done without my knowledge. It was an informal conversation. And it's not that I said this, that I stayed until September. The truth is a series of documents that we've shown. Namely, that I was in Sladara and that I functioned in Sladara first as the commissioner for refugees and then member of the Executive Board directly in charge of the Department for Internal Revenue, as it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to focus directly on my questions, where the notes say that you remained with your military unit until September we agree that's not true; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I mean it's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And where the note records in the fourth paragraph that you had told them you were not aware of the events surrounding the creation of the Crisis Staff or its later actions, that wouldn't be the truth either, would it?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff of the Serb Democratic Party is a staff that I created and as you said a moment ago, it was on the 8th of April that the Crisis Staff of Rogatica was formed and I was informed towards the end of April that I was a member and that's where I went. And everything that is written and that is different to that, is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the note reflects that you told the police were appointed head of income administration in September. Instead, you were appointed in June; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: No. The Crisis Staff, while it functioned, I was the commissioner for refugees. When the Executive Board was established, the Executive Board was joined by the member who is directly in charge of the revenue service, and I think that the Executive Board was established in September, and it was then that I was directly appointed to that line of work. Or was it October maybe? I wouldn't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the note states that you weren't present in Rogatica town between March and September 1992. That, again, isn't the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: It's not true. I don't know what they mean by Rogatica. Do they mean just the centre of town or the territory of the municipality? I was not in the centre of Rogatica because Muslims held Rogatica in that sense, and my house is 2 kilometres away from Sladara further to the north so --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir -- sir, I'm going to stop you there. In fact, your evidence is that you entered Rogatica town and took the video that you testified about on direct examination in late July or early August 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Came in, went out. I did not spend time there. My house is in a village that is further to the north from Sladara, so I did not stay in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'd put to you that however the note was compiled, in fact, almost nothing in it is true; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: That's the way it seems. I told you: Had they given this to me, had they asked me to sign it, I wouldn't have signed it. I had no influence whatsoever over the writing up of this note.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the note was taken in the context of an investigation into what happened in Rogatica in 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think -- I don't know. Whether they said specifically why they were involved in an investigation. Probably, probably the investigation was in the context of developments from 1992. That is to say, what was characteristic of Rogatica, the secondary school of Veljko Vlahovic, the Rasadnik greenhouse, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'd put to you that all of the errors in the note tend to distance you from what happened in Rogatica in 1992, and I'd put to you that that is because you didn't tell them the truth to avoid any responsibility yourself. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do have objections. I am not evading personal responsibility. I am aware of the times in which I lived. I am aware of the steps I took then. My resignation was precisely along those lines. Namely, that I was not in favour of the war option. I was not a person who wanted to take part in war operations as someone who was in a decision-making position who had a say in all of this. So what have you stated is not correct. What is perhaps true, in part, is that after my resignation, relations with Rajko Kusic were not the way they were before. I didn't want to know anything and I didn't want to go into the activities of the military at all. That is why I was given this line of work which was totally independent of the military and I only worked on that. That's why I said in my statement I was never at the secondary, I was never in Rasadnik, I was never at a single place where the army was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I move on, I'd tender this document. Clearly we don't intend to rely on the substance of the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31593 receives number P6910, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you just mentioned that you were never at Rasadnik. Rasadnik was just a couple of hundred metres away from the Sladara factory; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Rasadnik is, I think, half a kilometre away from Sladara. I go in that direction as I go to my home in the village, but, again, 300, 400 metres along the road that is close to Rasadnik, I never entered that facility while the police and the military were there, and I don't know who else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You knew during the war that there was what you describe in your statement as an army detention facility there; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did know. When Radomir Furtula's unit returned from Sarajevo my brother returned with that unit. Before the war, he was a misdemeanours judge, and I knew that through him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, that's -- that information is already in your statement which is why I tried to stop you. You knew the detention facility was there. It was on your way home every day, as you've just testified. Now, the Chamber has received evidence that people detained there were subjected to serious violent crimes, including crimes of sexual violence, that detainees were taken out and murdered by an officer in the Rogatica Brigade. So I'd put to you that you knew people there were being abused, and that's why you didn't want to see it, that's why you didn't want to go there. That's true; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: That's not true. I've already told you what the reason is. I am not contradicting your assertion, but I'm telling you that I don't know what happened. I just know through my brother that that is where Serb soldiers were detained too. Those who were late in arriving at the front line, and those who fled from the front line. And also Muslim prisoners, and let me not repeat all that, what I've already said, Cakic who spoke about the crimes against the Obradovics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the Trial Chamber has heard that at some points Muslims were also detained at the Sladara facility. Were you also unaware of that?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: We, in Sladara, had a Crisis Staff, and we had the Executive Board, and that was in the administration buildings of Sladara. As for the gate that we went through, it is certain that the army didn't go that way or the police, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall on one occasion, in the middle of June 1992, several busloads of Muslims from outside the Rogatica municipality being taken to the Sladara facility and transferring buses there?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, it's the position of the Prosecution that the Muslims on those buses were then taken to the area near the Sokolac-Rogatica municipality border and murdered. Can I take it you're also not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: Later I heard about that happening, but then I did not know, and I didn't see those buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it correct -- I just want to perfectly understand your answer. Is it correct that you heard that Muslims who had been transferred and had stopped at one point at the Sladara facility that was Crisis Staff headquarters had then been taken near the Sokolac-Rogatica border and murdered. You heard all of those things?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I hadn't heard of all of that. I heard of this happening. Who the Muslims were, from which area, when specifically, that I don't know. I just heard that this happened, and I heard about that considerably later. And I think that somebody was prosecuted for that, some of the Serbs who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me ask you a very specific question. Had you heard that they were transferred through the Sladara facility before they were killed?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, because you didn't visit any of the detention facilities in the Rogatica municipality, you aren't aware that many of the people detained there were civilians, are you?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I heard -- I heard -- actually, the information was that civilians were being asked to come to the secondary school to be shielded from the war operations. All loyal citizens were called upon to seek shelter at the school. That is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One of the people who called them was Rajko Kusic; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I heard too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could I take the witness back a few questions. You earlier said that when Mr. Traldi asked you whether you heard about the Muslims being transferred by buses and stopped at the Sladara. You said when Mr. Traldi asked you whether you heard all of those things he mentioned, you said: No, I hadn't heard of all of that. I heard of this happening. Now, what is "this" then? What you did hear happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically I heard that some Muslims were killed in that area, between Sokolac and Rogatica or Han Pijesak. Now whether there is some pit where this was done -- or that's what I heard. And then Muslims were brought there, but I don't know when and from where I really don't know about that because I heard about this later. And as I've already said, I think that somebody was prosecuted for these crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, your answer, you gave that answer in response to a question about Muslims passing through the Sladara facility. So the Muslims being killed, you link that to what was put to you in the question, if I understand you well? That is, Muslims going to the Sladara facility.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That killing did occur, and I'm not aware -- and I am aware of that. And that is the only killing in the area -- in this area, Sokolac-Han Pijesak-Rogatica, and that's why I linked all of that up. Not because I perhaps know that they went through Sladara. I already told you I don't know and I did not see the buses or the people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said you believed that it happened at a pit. That's called the Paklenik pit; right? P-a-k-l-e-n-i-k.

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, by the end of the war after Zepa fell, there were almost no Muslims left in Rogatica municipality at all?

utterances.speaker: SVETO VESELINOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, that completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you, but we need to turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Veselinovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for answering all the questions that were put to you, put to you by the party, put to you by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 13th of November, 9.30 in the morning, I see, again, in Courtroom III, although -- yes, apparently this has changed. We thought that we would sit in Courtroom I but apparently it's Courtroom III, 9.30. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of November, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.
